name: Cloud Posture Coworker
tagline: Review Terraform & cloud config — read-only, evidence first
description: An infrastructure-security reviewer for teams without a cloud security team. Scans Terraform and cloud configuration with open-source tools (trivy, checkov), reads your live cloud posture strictly read-only, and fixes what matters in the IaC — never by clicking around a console.

name: Dependency Audit Coworker
tagline: Vulnerable dependencies — audit, minimal upgrades, PRs
description: A dependency auditor for teams without a security team. Runs open-source vulnerability scanners (osv-scanner, npm audit, pip-audit, trivy) across your lockfiles, separates exploitable from theoretical, and ships minimal, test-verified upgrade PRs.

name: Security Coworker
tagline: Find and fix security issues — scan, triage, PR
description: A code-security reviewer for teams without a security team. Drives open-source scanners (semgrep, gitleaks), triages findings in the context of YOUR codebase, and owns the fix through to a reviewable pull request.

name: AppSec Reviewer
tagline: Reviews a change for what an attacker can reach, and hands back the fix
description: A security reviewer for pull requests, branches and working-tree changes. Reads the change in the context of the code that calls it, proves each finding by tracing untrusted input to the flaw, ranks by what an attacker gets rather than by scanner severity, and hands back a patch and a test for anything it confirms.

name: Data Analyst
tagline: Answers a business question from the warehouse, with the query shown
description: An analyst for business teams that works from the organisation's Databricks workspace. Asks Genie in plain language, shows the SQL that produced every number, pins metric definitions so next week's answer is computed the same way, and says plainly when the data cannot answer the question. Read-only, under Unity Catalog permissions.

name: Design Reviewer
tagline: Compares what shipped to what was designed, and says exactly where they differ
description: A design QA reviewer for the hand-off gap. Reads the Figma frame, screenshots the built page, and lists the differences in spacing, type, colour, states and copy. Runs an accessibility pass and a design-system drift audit on the same screen, and hands the findings back as a review note or Figma comments. It reviews; it does not change designs or code.

name: Incident Scribe
tagline: Keeps the record of a live incident so the postmortem starts from evidence
description: Sits alongside an incident and keeps the record — a timestamped, append-only timeline of what was observed, decided and tried, with the evidence attached — then drafts the status updates, the hand-off brief and the blameless postmortem from it. It reads and writes the record; it never operates the system.

name: Onboarding Guide
tagline: Answers "how does this work here?" from the docs we actually have, and says when they don't
description: The coworker a new joiner asks instead of interrupting the team. Answers from the company's own handbook, runbooks, READMEs and design docs, cites the document and section every time, names the owner when the answer is not written down, and keeps a running list of the documentation that contradicted itself along the way.

name: Wiz Security Analyst
tagline: Turns what Wiz found into what to fix first, and who fixes it
description: A cloud security analyst that works from your Wiz tenant. Ranks issues by whether an attacker can actually reach them, traces each one to the code and the team that owns it, and hands back the fix with the Wiz evidence attached. It writes to Wiz only when you hand it a security review to import.
